title: secure-readiness-labbook-ari-2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal labbook for SOC2 readiness — working through mapping, evidence harvest checklist, open questions, and small mitigation ideas. This is messy by design: capture thoughts, experiments, and what I need to ask infra/product owners. Not for wide distribution yet.

Current snapshot (high-level):
- Control areas I'm focusing on this sprint: Id&Access (SSO/MFA/KMS), Change Mgmt (deploy approvals, release notes), Logging & Detection (audit logs, alerting), Data Handling (PII classification + private deploy evidence), Availability & Capacity (Dedicated pools + SLA tests).
- Overall readiness: ~65% for the initial control set we intend to show auditors (security + availability + confidentiality). Lots of evidence exists but it's scattered across repos, cloud consoles, and private deployment docs.

Open questions / confidence checks (need answers from owners):
1) KMS key rotation cadence for customer keys used in Private deployments — do we have automated rotation? Owner: Lina. Evidence: key rotation logs? (Where exactly?)
2) When Dedicated GPUs are scaled down during off-peak, are there any persisted artifacts that would break retention evidence we claim? Owner: Infra (Devon).
3) Access review cadence for service accounts that run the serving runtime in prod clusters. Where is the list of service accounts?
4) Is there an internal runbook for restoring KV cache objects after failover? Auditors may ask about recovery procedures for inference state.

Control mapping brainstorm (rough):
- Access controls (TS 3 / Security): SSO enforced via Okta for all console access. MFA enforced for human users. For service-to-service auth we use mTLS + short-lived tokens (runtime-auth). Evidence to collect: Okta policy snapshots, SAML app config export, Okta sign-in logs for last 90 days, IAM role binding list (prod clusters).
- Cryptographic protections (TS / Confidentiality): Customer keys optionally managed by customer KMS for Private. Server-side encryption for hosted artifacts (S3) with KMS CMKs. Evidence: KMS audit log (Cloud KMS KeyRing), sample KMS policy, guidance doc for customer-supplied keys.
- Change management (TS / Processing integrity): PR approvals required for infra config changes. Release checklist for serving-runtime includes canary rollout and health checks. Evidence: Jira change ticket + PR linked + deployment timeline, rollout policy in console (screenshot).
- Logging & monitoring (TS / Availability & Security): Centralized audit logs in cloud logging + forwarded to SIEM. Alerting rules for runtime OOM, degraded latency SLOs. Evidence: example alert sent in last 30 days, retention policy doc, logging config.
- Data handling (TS / Confidentiality): For Private deployments, control ensures data stays in customer VPC and is not egressed. Evidence: VPC peering configs, network policy YAML, on-prem packaging manifest.

Evidence harvest plan (practical):
- Week 1: Collect exports (Okta, KMS, VPC configs) and stash in evidence-bucket/evidence-2026-03 (ACL: trust-ops-readonly). Responsible: Lina.
- Week 2: Pull recent deployment PRs and change ticket history for the last 6 months (ENG- labels). Responsible: Devon.
- Week 3: Run a small SLA test across regions (hosted API + Dedicated fallback) and record traces + latency charts. Responsible: me (Ari) + SRE.
- Ongoing: Evidence index doc (spreadsheet) mapping control -> artifact path -> owner -> short note.

Sample control-to-artifact rows (text table):
- Control: MFA enforcement | Artifact: Okta policy export (okta-mfa-policy-2026-02.json) | Owner: Lina | Where: confluence link / admin UI screenshot
- Control: KMS rotation | Artifact: Cloud KMS audit log excerpt | Owner: Lina | Note: need rotation proof for customer-managed keys
- Control: Deployment approvals | Artifact: Jira CHG-xxxx + PR#842 | Owner: Devon | Where: github + jira

Risks observed (and quick mitigation ideas):
- Risk: Evidence fragmentation slows audit response. Mitigation: short-term: central evidence bucket + checklist. Long-term: small rightsized evidence-collector lambda that grabs exports nightly.
- Risk: Private deployment evidence relies on customer configs (we may need attestation template). Mitigation: create an onboarding attestation checklist and include a signed artifact that customer returns.
- Risk: Service account sprawl. Mitigation: run an access inventory sweep, rotate keys, and remove unused roles.

To-dos (immediate):
- [ ] Create evidence-bucket skeleton and permissions (AWS ticket).
- [ ] Draft one-pager attestation template for Private deployments (2 slides max).
- [ ] Ask SRE for list of last 6 canary rollouts and link to artifacts.
- [ ] Pull sample Okta sign-in logs for last 90 days (export).
- [ ] Confirm log retention policy (how many days stored in plain cloud logging vs SIEM).

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Auditors like: concrete artifacts, tracerable ownership, retention statements, and a clear "what happened vs what should happen" during incidents. Keep evidence that shows both config and activity.
- When in doubt, include a screenshot + raw export (JSON/CSV) of the same item.
- Keep one index spreadsheet that points to sealed artifacts; don't move artifacts after you link them.

Mini experiments (ideas worth trying):
- Small script: gather Okta app config + recent sign-ins + list of active sessions; produce a single archive per quarter. Could be used for both audit and oncall.
- Canary replay: keep a recorded canary run (traces + latency) and store it as proof of availability testing.

Random snippets / reminders:
- Link to infra runbook PR for KV cache restore: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842
- Confluence workspace for attestation templates: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Attestation-Templates
- Jira change template: CHG-TEMPLATE-01

End of scratch - will iterate next time after getting Lina/Devon clarifications.

-- Ari

(If I stop here and come back: check Week 1 artifacts and add direct download links into index sheet)
